submission.natural_language_explanation: The pole detects a detached punctuation glyph: the token it peaks on is made only of punctuation/symbol characters — a typographic separator or symbol cluster, never a word (or a number) — and its strength is fixed by that one token, since layer 0 reads only the token and its position (token identity 99% of variance, position 0%; the words around it and the token after it have no effect). Strength is graded by glyph: the rule/bar/separator family is strongest (' —' 1.00, ' ―' 0.89, ' |' 0.89, ' /' 0.82, ' -' 0.78, ' –' 0.72, ' --' 0.71, ' •' 0.63 of max), bar/arrow/bracket clusters reach 0.25-0.55 (' //', ' ...', ' <-', ' [/', ' [+]', ' [-]', ' ---', ' │', ' ||', ' ├', ' ├──', ' ►', ' ●'), while detached sentence punctuation and operators stay at or below 0.2 and usually at 0 (' .', ' ,', ' :', ' ;', ' )', ' (', ' +', ' =', ' &', ' >', ' ?', ' *', ' $', ' %', ' !' 0.18, ' #' 0.18), and the same glyph without its leading space is not detected at all (bare '-', '–', '—', '/', '.', ',', ':' give 0), the exceptions being bare '|' (0.44) and glued code-punctuation clusters ('","', '=/', ')|', '[/' at 0.35-0.48); the only non-punctuation leftovers are ' https' (0.49) and a couple of code words (' sudo', ' alias', 0.30).

rival_explanations: It is a plain token-identity lookup for the few detached separators that dominate the scan (' —', ' |', ' /', ' --', ' –', ' -', ' //', ' ...') and generalises to nothing else, so rarer members of the same visual family (' ―', ' •', ' │', ' ├', ' [+]', ' ●', ' ►') should sit at zero.

It fires on any non-alphanumeric token, detached sentence punctuation and operators included, so ' ,', ' .', ' :', ' ;', ' )', ' +', ' =', ' &', ' >' and ' ?' with a leading space should be active and should make a text predicted active.

What matters is the leading space rather than the glyph: it fires on any space-prefixed token that is not a plain lower-case word, so ' !', ' #', ' @', ' ~', ' _', ' <' and ' %' should be strongly active.
